la:verb:perterreo.html:
per-terrĕo, ui, ĭtum, 2, v. a.,
to frighten or terrify thoroughly: aliquem,: alios magnitudine poenarum,; : metu perterriti,: obstupefactus ac perterritus,: maleficii conscientiā perterritus,: ossa mea perterrita sunt, (but the true read., , is proterritus).

senses: to disturb or perturb, trouble or alarm
la:verb:perturbo.html:
per-turbo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to throw into confusion or disorder, to confuse, disturb (cf.: confundo, misceo).
Lit.: omnia,: provinciam,: aetatum ordinem,: condiciones pactionesque bellicas perjurio,: dies intermissus aut nox interposita saepe perturbat omnia,: reliquos (milites) incertis ordinibus perturbaverunt,: aciem,: domum,.—Pass., .—
Transf., to mix or mingle together: omnia subtiliter cretā permisceas cum salibus torrefactis ac tritis et diu oleo injecto perturbes,.—
Trop., to disturb, discompose, embarrass, confound: mea consilia,: mentes animosque perturbat timor,: clamore perturbari,: animum, joined with concitare,: de rei publicae salute perturbari,: haec te vox non perculit? non perturbavit?: magno animi motu perturbatus,.—Hence, perturbātus, a, um, P. a.
Troubled, disturbed, unquiet: mihi civitatem perturbatam vestris legibus et contionibus et deductionibus tradidistis,: perturbatissimum tempestatis genus,: flamma quassatae rei publicae perturbatorumque temporum,,

73.—

Disturbed, embarrassed, discomposed: homo perturbatior metu,: sane sum perturbatus cum ipsius familiaritate,.—Subst.: per-turbāta, ōrum, n., confused visions, perverted truths: nunc onusti cibo et vino perturbata et confusa cernimus,.—Adv.: perturbātē, confusedly, disorderly: ne quid perturbate, ne quid contorte dicatur,; : muta animalia perturbate moveri,.

la:verb:pertineo.gloss: to extend, stretch out, reach, matter
senses: to extend, stretch out, reach, matter
to belong, relate, pertain, have concern
to have a tendency to, tend to
to apply to, be applicable to, suit, be suitable to
to be the property of, belong to; to be attributable to
la:verb:pertineo.html:
per-tĭnĕo, ŭi, 2, v. n.
teneo
,
to stretch out, reach, extend to a place; to arrive at a place (class., esp. in the trop. signif.); constr. with ad and acc., or with advv.; very rarely with in or per and acc.;v.infra.
Lit.: aspera arteria ad pulmones usque pertinet,: venae in omnes partes corporis pertinentes,: deus pertinens per naturam cujusque rei, etc.,: Belgae pertinent ad inferiorem partem fluminis Rheni,: rivi, qui ad mare pertinebant,: hanc (silvam) longe introrsus pertinere,: in vastae magnitudinis urbe partium sensu non satis pertinente in omnia,extending in all directions, Weissenb. ad loc.; cf.: quod ait praetor: pertinet, hoc significat: quod ex aedibus ejus in tuas pertinet, hoc est dirigitur, extenditur, pervenit,.—
Trop.
To reach, extend (like διήκειν, καθήκειν): eadem bonitas etiam ad multitudinem pertinet,: caritas patriae per omnes ordines pertinebat,i. e. pervaded,: ad posteritatis memoriam pertinere,: fulmina, quorum significatio ad totam vitam pertinet,: hic pertinet a natali ad diem extremum,.—
To belong, relate, concern, pertain or have reference to, affect any thing: somnium ad aliquam rem pertinet,: illa res ad meum officium pertinet,: nihil ad patriciam Sulpiciorum familiam Quirinius pertinuit,: haec breviter attingemus, scrutati maxime pertinentia,.—
To have a tendency, to tend or lead to an object or result, : illud quo pertineat, videte,; : quod autem plures a nobis nominati sunt, eo pertinuit, quod, etc.,: summa illuc pertinet, ut sciatis, etc.,: interpretando, quorsum quidque pertineat,: quid ista ad vidulum pertinent, servae sint istae an liberae?.—Esp. in phrase: quod ad aliquem (aliquid) pertinet, as far as concerns, in regard to (mostly post-Aug.): quod ad inducias pertineret, sic belli rationem esse divisam, ut, etc., * : quod ad nationes exteras pertinet, Cicero varie,: quod ad Dymnum pertinet, nihil scio,: quod pertinet ad elephantos, id.

9, 2, 19; cf.: quantum ad decernentes pertinet,: quod ad me pertinet, intellego me perdidisse, etc.,; ; ; : cum virtutibus tum etiam fortuna, siquid hoc ad rem pertinet,: quatenus quidque se attingat ad seque pertineat perspicere,: illud dissimulas ad te quod pertinet,. —

To apply to, be applicable to, to suit, be suitable to a person or thing: magis pol haec malitia pertinet ad viros, quam ad mulieres,: ad quem suspicio maleficii pertineat,on whom suspicion should fall,: ad officium meum,: liberalitas ad rem familiarem meam,: ad imperatorem prodigium pertinere,.—
To belong, be the right of (usu. of a right, as opp. to possession): sed regnum ad se et ad matrem suam pertinere arbitrabantur,: ad quem jure regnum pertinet,: bona ad me pertinent, solus enim sum filius defuncti,: Europa jam, dubio procul, jure ad Romanos pertinebat,: (Armenia) quae antea ad majores suos pertinuisse monstrabat,.—
To belong, to be the property of (late Lat.): omnia quae ad se pertinebant,; ; .—Hence, adv.: pertĭnenter, aptly, suitably, appositely, pertinently (post-class.): pertinenter ad causam,.—Comp.: pertinentius,.—Sup.: pertinentissime,.

la:verb:pertimesco.html:
per-tĭmesco, mŭi, 3,
v. inch. a. and n., to become very much frightened, to be greatly afraid of any thing, to fear greatly: si tantam religionem non pertimescebas, etc.,: id vero non mediocriter pertimesco,: nomen imperii etiam in levi personā pertimescitur,: fames esset pertimescenda,: non putavi famam inconstantiae mihi pertimescendam,: ne quid peccasset, pertimescebat,: nec illi umquam de se pertimescent,: graviter de suis periculis fortunisque omnibus pertimescunt,; so, de aliquā re,.— Absol., ; .

la:verb:pertimeo.gloss: to fear greatly, to be very timid
senses: to fear greatly, to be very timid
la:verb:pertimeo.html:
per-tĭmĕo, ŭi, 2, v. n.,
to fear greatly, to be very timid, : non pertimentes ullam perturbationem, Pet. 3, 6 (al. praetim).

la:noun:perturbatio.html:
perturbātĭo, ōnis, f.
perturbo
,
confusion, disorder, disturbance.
Lit.: caeli (opp. serenitas),: hostium,.—
Trop.
In gen., political disturbance, disorder, revolution: quid est enim aliud tumultus nisi perturbatio tanta, ut major timor oriatur?: quantas perturbationes et quantos aestus habet ratio comitiorum?: cum enim omnes post interitum Caesaris novarum perturbationum causae quaeri viderentur,: videtis, quo in motu temporum, quantā in conversione rerum ac perturbatione versemur,: magna totius exercitūs perturbatio facta est,.—
Mental or personal disturbance, disquiet, perturbation: motus atque perturbatio animorum atque rerum,: vitae et magna confusio,: rationis,: valetudinis,.—
In partic., an emotion, passion: quae Graeci πάθη vocant, nobis perturbationes appellari magis placet, quam morbos, : est igitur Zenonis haec definitio, ut perturbatio sit aversa a rectā ratione, contra naturam animi commotio: quidam brevius perturbationem esse appetitum vehementiorem,: ex quā (vitiositate) concitantur perturbationes, quae sunt turbidi animorum concitatique motus, aversi a ratione et inimicissimi mentis vitaeque tranquillae,: perturbationes sunt genere quatuor, partibus plures, aegritudo, formido, libido, laetitia,: impetu quodam animi et perturbatione magis, quam judicio aut consilio regi,: perturbationem afferre,: in perturbationes atque exanimationes incidere,; opp. to tranquillitas,.

la:noun:pertinacia.html:
pertĭnācĭa, ae, f.
pertinax
,
perseverance, constancy, in a good sense; and (more freq.) in a bad sense, obstinacy, pertinacity (syn.: perseverantia, pervicacia): dicitur quom demonstratur in quo non debet pertendi et pertendit, pertinaciam esse; in quo oportet manere, si in eo perstet, perseverantia sit, Müll.; cf.: unicuique virtuti finitimum vitium reperietur, ut pertinacia, quae perseverantiae finitima est,; v. Att. ap. : certamen instituit non pertinaciā et studio vincendi, sed, etc.,: desistere pertinaciā,: pertinaciae finem facere,: muliebri pertinacia accendi,: pertinaciam alicujus vincere,.—In a good sense, : patientia et pertinacia hostis,: in evitando inevitabili malo,, praef. 12: auctorum pertinacia,steadfast opinion,.—Personified, the sister of Æther and Dies, .

la:adj:pertenuis.html:
per-tĕnŭis, e, adj.,
very thin, very small or fine.
Lit.: sabulum pertenue,.—
Trop., very slight or slender, very weak: spes salutis,: discrimen,: suspicio,: argumentum,: ars,.

la:verb:pertaedet.html:
per-taedet, taesum est, 2 (quidam pertisum volunt:
quod consuetudo non probavit,; cf. Fest. pp. 216 sq.; 273, 8 Müll.; also Paul. ex Müll.), v. impers. and n., to be disgusted or wearied with any thing; to feel disgust at, be sick of.
With gen.: me sermonis pertaesum est,: quem pertaesum est esse domi,: pertaesum est enim (me) levitatis,: pertaesum est vos injuriae, Dietsch: negotii,: duas uxores habuerat, quarum matrimonii pertaedebat,: lentitudinis eorum pertaesa,.—
With dat.: usque adeo pertaesum vos mihi esse, Gracch. ap. P.—
With acc.: pertaesus ignaviam suam,: pertaesus morum perversitatem ejus,; .

la:adj:pertinax.html:
per-tĭnax, ācis, adj.
tenax
,
that holds fast, that clings firmly, very tenacious.
Lit. (only poet. and in post-Aug. prose): digitus male pertinax,: ales unguibus pertinax,: tenaxne pater ejus est? Ph. Pater immo edepol pertinax, exceedingly avaricious, .—
Transf., that lasts long, very durable: spiritus,: siligo in Allobrogum agro pertinax,.—
Trop., firm, constant, steadfast, persevering, unyielding; in a bad sense, obstinate, pertinacious, stubborn (cf. pervicax); constr. absol., with in and abl.; also (rare and not ante-Aug.) with in and acc., adversus and acc., ad and acc.; also (post-Aug.) with gen., Att. ap. : concertationes in disputando pertinaces,: pertinacissimus fueris, si, etc.,: valde pertinax,: pertinax fama,: studium, prooem.: certamen,: stare pertinaci statu,: octoginta milia fortissimae pertinacissimaeque in retinendis armis juventutis,: pertinax virtus,: pertinax adversus temerarios impetus,: pertinacior in repugnando,: pertinax ad obtinendam injuriam,: in quod coepit pertinax et intenta,.—
Poet., with inf.: fortuna ... Ludum insolentem ludere pertinax,.—
With gen.: justitiae,: irae,.—Hence, adv.: pertĭnācĭter.
Very fast or firmly, very tenaciously, persistently: haec ipsa magis pertinaciter haerent, quo deteriora sunt,; : pertinacius resistere,: pertinacissime retinere,. —
Constantly, firmly, steadily, perseveringly; obstinately, stubbornly, pertinaciously: pertinaciter liberalibus studiis deditus,: pertinaciter in aliquā re manere,: pertinaciter offensus, Planc. ap. : contendere,: studere,.—Comp.: pertinacius insequi,.—Sup.: pertinacissime pabulo abstinere,; .—
Pertĭnax, ācis, m., surname of the emperor P. Helvius, who succeeded Commodus on the throne, ; .

la:verb:pertracto.html:
per-tracto (pertrecto), āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to touch, feel, handle any thing (class.).
Lit.: papillam,: mullos,: bestias manibus, Auct. B. afr. 72: arma,: caput dormienti,: corpus hominis,.—
Trop., to busy or occupy one's self with any thing, to handle, treat, to investigate, study any thing: mentem omni cogitatione pertractans,: sensus mentesque hominum,: narrationem,: ad totam philosophiam pertractandam se dare,: pertractare ea quae rem continent,: primum quae scripsi mecum ipse pertracto,: pertractare visu vulnera,to explore, scan,: mente, .—Hence, * per-tractātē, adv., in a well-considered manner, elaborately, systematically: nam pertractate facta est (fabula),i. e. with a moral in view,.

la:verb:pertendo.html:
per-tendo, di, sum, and tum, 3, v. a., and n.—Prop., to stretch out, extend

hence, transf., *

Act., to carry out, go on with, perform any thing: video non licere ut coeperam hoc pertendere,.—
Neutr.
Prop., to strive forward, to push on to a place; hence, to go right on, proceed to (not in Cic. or Cæs.; ap. , the correct reading is perpendemus): pars maxima Romam pertenderunt,: pertendit ad alteram ripam,; id. Vit. Plin.; .—
Trop., to keep on, persevere, persist: verum si incipies, neque pertendes naviter,: a qua re sit pertinacia quom quaeritur, ostenditur esse a pertendendo ... in quo non debet pertendi, etc., Müll.; (3, 7), 17.—
To attend, be attentive (late Lat.), Laurent. Hom. 1.
la:verb:pertendo.inflection: di, sum, and tum, 3, v. a., n.

la:verb:pertingo.gloss: to stretch or reach out; to extend
senses: to stretch or reach out; to extend
la:verb:pertingo.html:
per-tingo, ĕre, v. a.
tango
,
to stretch out, reach, extend to a certain point (rare; not in Cic.; often confounded in MSS. with pertineo).
Lit.: collis in immensum pertingens, Dietsch and Kritz: montis Apennini jugum mediā curvaturā prope tangens oras maris Hadriani pertingit circumitionibus contra fretum,: infortunatam pertingens cespite Trojam,: turris, cujus culmen pertingat ad caelum,; al. (but in , the correct read. is perterget, v. Lachm. ad h. l.).—
Trop., to reach, attain: ad sapientiam Zenonis pertingere,.

la:verb:pertranseo.html:
per-transĕo, īvi, īre, v. n.,
to go or pass through (post-Aug.).
Lit.: cum viridis aspectus (smaragdi), non pertransit,: terram, et saep.—
Transf.
To go or pass by (late Lat.; not in ), : Levita, cum esset secus locum et videret eum, pertransiit,.—
To pass away: donec pertranseat indignatio,.

la:verb:pertraho.gloss: to draw, drag, bring or conduct forcibly to a place
senses: to draw, drag, bring or conduct forcibly to a place
to entice, lure or allure to a place; lead astray or away
la:verb:pertraho.html:
per-trăho, xi, ctum, 3, v. a.,
to draw or drag, to bring or conduct forcibly to a place (not in Cic. or Cæs.).
Lit.: aliquem in castra,: ratem ad ripam,: pertractus ad Vitellium,: mulierem Romam ad centumviros,: patriam suam in jus, ad aliam civitatem, ext.: aliquem intra moenia vinctum,, n. 8.—
To entice, allure to a place: in locum iniquum pertractus,: hostem ad insidiarum locum,.—
Transf., to draw out, extract: virus,. —
Trop., to lead away, lead astray: sui erroris arbitrio pertrahere et alios multos, Mos. et Rom. Leg. Coll. 15, 3, 1.

la:adj:pertristis.html:
per-tristis, e, adj.,
very sad or mournful.
Lit.: carmen, Cic. poët. Div. 1, 8, 14.—
Transf., very austere or morose: patruus,.

la:verb:perterebro.html:
per-tĕrĕbro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to bore through: columnam,: lapis perterebratus,; .

senses: A Roman cognomen — famously held by

la:noun:pertractatio.html:
pertractātĭo and pertrectātĭo, ōnis, f.
pertracto, a touching; hence trop.
,
A handling: partium aegrarum,.—
A handling, i. e. an occupying or busying one's self with any thing, application to any thing: poëtarum,: rerum publicarum,.

la:verb:pertexo.html:
per-texo, xui, xtum, 3, v. a.
Lit.
To weave throughout, weave entirely: palla bysso tenui pertexta, i. e. byssina,.—
To interweave, i. e. to furnish, decorate, adorn with any thing: Odeum, quod Pericles navium malis et antennis pertexuit, dub. (al. pertexit).—
Trop., to go through with, perform, accomplish: inceptum dictis,: locum,: pertexe modo quod exorsus es,.

la:verb:pertento.html:
per-tento, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a., to feel all over; hence,
To prove, try, test any thing.
Lit. (very rare): cum utrumque pugionem pertentasset,: alta bipenni latera, Petr. poët. 89, v. 24.—
Trop. (rare but class.): aliquem,: animum cohortis,: rem, to consider or weigh well, : omnia pertento, omnia experior,: nobilium adulescentium animos,.—
To pervade, invade; to seize, affect (poet. and in postAug. prose): dum prima lues ... Pertentat sensus,: pertentant gaudia pectus,: tremor pertentet Corpora,: vinolentiā ac fatigatione pertentatus,.

la:adj:perterricrepus.html:
perterrĭcrĕpus, a, um, adj.
perterreo-crepo
,
that clatters or rattles most terribly (ante-class.); old poët. ap. : sonitus,.
